One brief. Agent-built workflows. No human intervention.

Powered byGemus

Abstract

As multimodal resources are transformed into media outputs, agentic AI is expected to stay aligned with design intent over long horizons. Designers follow briefs specifying goals, constraints, and deliverables, with later work building on earlier decisions. Recent work reuses design experience across tasks, yet alignment among artifacts within one project remains challenging. Agents therefore need to preserve and apply this intent across domains and as projects grow. We introduce Design Anything, a graph-based harness that preserves design intent outside the model and binds deliverables to the workflow steps that produce them through an intent–execution graph. A task contract retains constraints and decisions, selected designs become explicit inputs to later generations, and a deterministic controller uses bindings and execution records to check output types and counts, identify outstanding deliverables, and guide subsequent turns. We also introduce DesignAnything-Bench, with 228 tasks across 19 design domains, including 38 project families at scales of 6, 14, and 24 artifacts. With the LLM held fixed, Design Anything satisfies 85.0% and 92.5% of the brief's factual constraints with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash High and GPT-5.6 Sol High, respectively, exceeding the strongest same-model baselines by 15.4% and 14.4%. These gains reach 25.1% and 23.0% on 24-artifact tasks. Under each model, Design Anything leads or ties in constraint satisfaction in 18 of 19 domains. Professional designers also prefer its complete deliverable sets over those of same-model baselines in a blind evaluation.

Original brief

Read the full brief

LUMA | AI glasses and a charging case for everyday transitions

We are developing LUMA for adults who want to capture a moment during an urban pause and move comfortably between work and leisure. The system comprises one complete pair of AI glasses and one matching charging/storage case. Connected assistance uses an intentionally captured image and a short, user-initiated spoken question through a paired phone. The glasses themselves are the main design task: two clear non-display lenses, a complete frame, folding temples, integrated electronics, comfortable contact surfaces and reachable physical controls. Print "LUMA" on the glasses and case.

The glasses mass target is at most 42 g. Choose a front width of 140–150 mm and a hinge-axis-to-tip centreline length of 135–150 mm for each temple; the largest temple section is at most 18 mm high and 12 mm thick. Folded glasses fit within 150 × 60 × 48 mm; the closed case fits within 170 × 85 × 65 mm, with at least 2 mm cavity clearance on each opposing side of the chosen folded envelope. Use the eleven recorded electronic modules, with 1 mm between envelopes and 1 mm enclosure outside them except at functional openings. The right-temple underside carries two flush pads of diameter 2 mm, spaced 6 mm centre to centre, both within 60 mm of the hinge; P+ is nearer the hinge. Matching case tips have diameter 1.2 mm. Use satin TR90 for the frame and temple shells, anodised aluminium hinges and silicone nose and ear contact surfaces. Develop the colour palette. Make B01 accessible for user replacement and print "User-replaceable B01" beside its removal detail.

The three glasses states are READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY. READY exposes the camera with its indicator off; CAPTURE exposes the camera with a steady white front indicator; PRIVACY closes an opaque slider over the camera and disables camera and microphone capture. Give the slider a visible position mark. Folded glasses dock with the slider closed; the case indicator is steady amber during charging and off during stored/idle. Its indicator remains visible with the lid closed. Label these states on their corresponding design boards.

Audience: the product owner, industrial design team and engineering team, choosing the complete eyewear concept and preparing its first development brief.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the shared product, fit, operation, material and context facts. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists each deliverable's proportion, format and stage. 03-module-records.md contains the eleven electronic module records. module-envelopes.en.md gives their local dimensions and permitted regions. charging-interface.en.md records pad geometry and mating relationships. module-and-docking-constraints.png diagrams the module envelopes and local charging interface. wearer-contact-map.png supplies the shared wearer and contact-zone reference across the directions. everyday-pause-reference.png supplies atmosphere for an urban pause and a warm office desk.

Deliverables: 1. Three distinct complete-product direction boards, each showing the glasses open and folded beside their matching case 2. One written selection sheet naming the chosen direction and the frame, temple and case decisions carried forward 3. Two specification sheets: a component and state sheet listing all eleven module IDs, envelope dimensions, connections, selected dimensions, pad-centre positions and operating-state changes; a material zoning and finish sheet listing materials, surface treatments, colour codes and contact zones 4. Six selected-glasses anatomy and detail boards: one front/top/right orthographic and component anatomy with schematic wiring and B01 replacement explosion; one front three-quarter view; one rear three-quarter view; one folded underside view; one nose-contact detail; and one ear-contact and hinge detail 5. Five operation and wearing boards: W1 everyday in READY with a nose/ear inset; CAPTURE with button reach and the white indicator; W2 work pause in PRIVACY with the closed slider and button inhibition; W3 commute pause in READY with a clear temple side view; and W4 cafe pause in PRIVACY with folded glasses held above the open case before contact 6. Four case boards: open charging with module placement, contact section and cavity dimensions; closed stored/idle with an empty open-case inset and outer dimensions; an enlarged empty-case interior; and a removal sequence with the fully folded glasses lifted by the frame/temple region 7. One material and colour application board for the selected glasses and case, mapping the material specification onto exterior, interior and skin-contact surfaces 8. One 12-second use-and-storage video moving through READY, CAPTURE, PRIVACY, folded docking with amber charging indication and closed-case stored/idle 9. One development presentation of at least 12 pages, reusing the directions, selection, both specifications, anatomy, details, operation, case and material work

Acceptance: - On the three direction boards, present three named alternatives before the selection sheet; on that sheet and the presentation's first page, identify one selected direction, then develop its frame, temples and case in both specifications and every subsequent application. - On the component specification, orthographic anatomy, folded underside and case boards, repeat the same selected open/folded dimensions and pad-centre positions. Dimension the 140–150 mm front-width range, 135–150 mm temple-length range, 18 × 12 mm section limit, 150 × 60 × 48 mm folded limit, 170 × 85 × 65 mm case limit and at least 2 mm cavity clearance on all six sides except marked support/contact interfaces; match openings, seams and hinge positions across all six anatomy/detail boards. - On the component specification and orthographic anatomy, repeat all eight glasses module IDs, recorded envelopes and local-axis orientations; on that specification and the open charging board, repeat CB01, CC01 and U01 and their recorded envelopes. Show 1 mm envelope separation and enclosure, K01's 4 mm aperture, I01 within 12 mm of its centre, and B01's access cover, detachable connection and removal arrow labelled User-replaceable B01 on the anatomy board. - On the component specification, operation boards, video and presentation, repeat READY, CAPTURE and PRIVACY with the prescribed camera, light and slider states. Label W1, W2, W3 and W4 on their assigned boards; show the W1 and W3 contact placements matching the nose/ear detail boards, button inhibition in W2, and folded glasses with the shutter closed and charging indication off before contact in W4. - On the charging and folded underside boards, repeat the 2 mm pads, 6 mm spacing, 1.2 mm case tips and chosen pad-centre distances within 60 mm of the right hinge, with P+ nearer the hinge. Across the four case boards and video, preserve the keyed seat, parallel mating faces, lens-clear frame supports and removal access; show amber charging indication after docking and the visible indicator off in closed stored/idle. - On the material specification, material application board and presentation, repeat satin TR90 shells, anodised aluminium hinges, silicone contacts and the selected colour codes; apply them consistently across the six anatomy/detail boards, five operation/wearing boards, four case boards and video. Show LUMA on the glasses and case, and reuse those labelled views with both specifications in the presentation's minimum 12 pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.

direction selection

# LUMA — Direction Selection Sheet **Document type:** presentation document; **stage:** process; **format:** A4. **No images.** This written record closes the direction phase and releases the selected concept into development. --- ## Page 1 — Direction selection ### 1. Purpose This sheet records the closure of the LUMA direction phase and releases the selected concept into development. It states the selected direction, the alternatives shown, the reasons for selection, and the locked schedule that all later work must repeat. ### 2. Alternatives shown The three alternatives were presented in the following order. #### 2.1 (A) Continuum — seamless minimal Continuum is a monobloc brow line with no visible parting seam, a flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover, satin graphite TR90 with a bone-white inner rim, one slim machined shutter track with a visible position mark, and a soft rounded pebble case in the matching graphite tone. #### 2.2 (B) Softline — rounded organic Softline uses generous radii, a warm sand TR90 shell with a clay inner rim and a soft-touch temple, a sculpted shutter ridge, and a case with a wrapped textile-look lid. #### 2.3 (C) Precision — engineered Precision uses an exposed anodised aluminium hinge barrel, crisp graphic seam lines, ink blue and graphite TR90 with silver metal, a recessed pocket around the charging pads, and a case with an exposed machined contact block. ### 3. Decision Selected direction: Continuum — seamless minimal. ### 4. Status of other directions Softline and Precision are retained for reference only and are not developed further. --- ## Page 2 — Why Continuum ### 1. Reasoning for selection Continuum is selected because its unbroken brow and buried hinge cover produce one continuous surface with no seam and no exposed barrel. This suits a product handled in an office and on the street: it reads as a complete object rather than an assembly of parts, and it gives fewer places for clothing, hair or desk surfaces to catch on visible mechanisms. The graphite and bone satin TR90 palette is quiet enough to pass as ordinary eyewear while the LUMA family is still recognisable. The bone inner rim gives a single controlled accent exactly where the wearer sees it when the glasses are folded. The rounded pebble case extends the same surface language to the dock, so the closed case reads as part of the same object rather than as a separate accessory. These choices support the fixed product intent: a complete adult-use AI glasses concept with a matching charging/storage case, deliberate capture initiation, and everyday wearing contexts. ### 2. Softline Softline was not carried forward because its warm tactile palette and wrapped textile lid move away from the neutral product language established for LUMA. The wrapped lid also adds a surface that collects dirt in the handled case routine. Its rounded organic language is coherent, but it would make the product family less directly comparable to the selected graphite and bone material direction. ### 3. Precision Precision was not carried forward because, although coherent, its exposed hinge barrel, graphic seams and recessed pad pocket read as more mechanical than an everyday brief asks for. The exposed barrel and graphic seams would draw attention to assembly details that Continuum resolves into a continuous surface. Its machined contact block and recessed pad pocket are technically legible, but they are less consistent with the quiet wearable form selected for LUMA. ### 4. Continuity with product requirements Continuum remains within the fixed requirements: two clear non-display lenses, a frame with one bridge and two nose-contact regions, two folding temples and two ear-contact regions, a camera at one outer front-frame corner, an opaque physical privacy shutter, a flush capture control, user-replaceable B01 in the left temple, and a case with internal charging contacts and a closed-lid indicator. It also preserves the required product marking LUMA on the glasses and case and the required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01. --- ## Page 3 — Frame decisions carried forward ### 1. Statement of intent The frame will carry the Continuum form language: a calm, continuous front that looks like ordinary eyewear, with the camera, indicator, microphone and shutter integrated without turning the front into a technical display. ### 2. Frame decisions | Item | Decision | | --- | --- | | Lens configuration | Two clear non-display lenses. | | Frame configuration | One bridge with two nose-contact regions, two folding temples and two ear-contact regions. | | Brow | Monobloc brow line with no visible parting seam. | | Inner rim | Bone-white inner rim, matching LUMA-C02 Bone in satin TR90. | | Hinge cover | Flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover. | | Front width | Open front width, hinge axis to hinge axis: 146 mm (permitted range 140 to 150 mm). | | Camera | K01 at the outer front corner of the right frame, forward-facing; clear optical aperture diameter 4 mm. | | Capture indicator | I01 beside K01 on the front, outward; centre 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre, within 12 mm, visible when the shutter is closed. | | Shutter | Opaque slider over the camera; travel 9 mm; visible position mark; closed position is PRIVACY. | | Microphone | M01 in the frame or forward temple, opening outward, away from skin and the hinge. | | Materials | Frame and temple shells in TR90, satin finish; hinges in anodised aluminium. | | Skin contact | Nose-contact surfaces in silicone LUMA-C04 Smoke, smooth rounded transitions, separated from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads. | ### 3. State relationship The frame must support the three operating states. In READY, the camera aperture is uncovered and the front capture indicator is off; no active capture is present. In CAPTURE, the aperture is uncovered, the front capture indicator is steadily white during the illustrated active interval, and the visible user-operated capture button is used for active capture. In PRIVACY, the entire aperture is covered by the opaque physical slider, the indicator is off, a visible physical position mark is present, camera and microphone capture are disabled, and pressing capture does not start capture. ### 4. Marking The required product marking LUMA appears on the glasses. The required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01 is carried with the left-temple battery service arrangement. --- ## Page 4 — Temple decisions carried forward ### 1. Statement of intent The temples will be slim, straight and tapered, so the glasses remain ordinary in silhouette while the modules, hinge and charging interface are contained cleanly. ### 2. P+ centre 18 mm and P- centre 24 mm behind the hinge axis, both within 60 mm of the hinge, P+ nearer the hinge. | | Battery service | B01 left battery envelope in the left temple; user-accessible cover, detachable connection and illustrated removal direction; required wording User-replaceable B01. | ### 3. Envelope separation is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes, and enclosure allowance is at least 1 mm outside each solid envelope except at its functional opening. Speaker openings are outward/downward near the ears, and the ear canals remain open. Ear-contact surfaces use silicone LUMA-C04 Smoke with smooth rounded transitions. ### 4. Service and handling The temple form keeps skin-contact zoning separate from sharp edges, open ports and charging pads. The two-pad docking is local to the underside of the right temple and does not alter the complete temple or case forms. Docking occurs with the glasses fully folded and the privacy slider closed. The selected pad positions remain within the first 60 mm from the hinge axis towards the tip. --- ## Page 5 — Case decisions carried forward ### 1. Statement of intent The case will be a rounded pebble dock in the same Continuum surface language, holding the folded glasses securely, exposing the charging interface only where needed, and reading as part of the same product family. ### 2. Case decisions | Item | Decision | | --- | --- | | Form | Rounded pebble form. | | Shell | Graphite shell. | | Marking | Bone-white LUMA print on the lid. | | Lid gap | Single fine meeting gap. | | Seat | Formed keyed seat that holds the folded frame clear of the lenses. | | Contact tips | Two contact tips, diameter 1.2 mm, centres 6 mm apart, matching polarity, parallel contact faces. | | Internal cavity | 154 by 64 by 48 mm. | | Closed envelope | 168 by 78 by 62 mm. | | Indicator | Front-edge indicator that stays visible with the lid closed. | | Module set | CB01, CC01, U01. | | Materials | Case materials and finishes selected in the design; LUMA-C05 Warm Grey flocked case tray. | ### 3. Docking and charging The docking orientation uses a visible locating/keying feature identifying the matching orientation. In the docking state the glasses are fully folded and the privacy slider is closed. In the charging state the glasses are seated, both pads are mated, and the separate case indicator is steadily amber. In the stored/idle state the same glasses are seated, the case indicator is off, and the case is closed. The case support uses frame/temple regions; lenses remain clear of direct supporting pressure. The closed-lid relationship contains all components within the closed case. Removal access provides finger access to frame/temple regions. The empty-case state presents an open cavity with the same supports, contacts and locating feature. ### 4. Case modules and power CB01 is the case battery envelope, CC01 is the case charging-board envelope, and U01 is the case input connector envelope. U01 is a USB-C-shaped input-connector envelope with its socket mouth exposed at the case wall. The case charging context is unplugged operation from its internal battery. The internal cavity clearance per side of the folded envelope is 3.5 mm width, 6 mm depth, 4 mm height; the minimum is 2 mm on every opposing side, and the formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm charge-contact tips are the explicit local exceptions marked as support and charging-contact interfaces. --- ## Page 6 — Locked schedule This table is the authoritative record that the two specification sheets and every later board repeat. | No. | Locked schedule entry | |---:|---| | 1 | Selected direction: Continuum — seamless minimal. Fixed by the selection The direction is fixed as Continuum — seamless minimal. Softline and Precision are retained for reference only and are not developed further. The locked schedule is fixed and must be repeated without change. The glasses use two clear non-display lenses, a monobloc brow with no visible parting seam, a bone-white inner rim, a flush buried anodised aluminium hinge cover, a right-front camera with a 4 mm clear optical aperture, a capture indicator 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre, an opaque 9 mm shutter slider with a visible position mark and PRIVACY closed position, and a flush right-temple capture button 42 mm behind the hinge axis. The temples use the selected 142 mm length and 16 mm by 10 mm largest section. The right temple carries the two flush charging pads with P+ at 18 mm and P- at 24 mm behind the hinge axis. The case uses the rounded pebble form, graphite shell, bone-white LUMA lid print, keyed seat, 1.2 mm contact tips at 6 mm spacing, internal cavity 154 by 64 by 48 mm, and closed envelope 168 by 78 by 62 mm. The palette is fixed as LUMA-C01 through LUMA-C05. ### 2. Fixed by the component records The module set for the glasses is C01, B01, B02, S01, S02, K01, M01 and I01. The case module set is CB01, CC01 and U01. Quantities are exactly as recorded. Envelope orientation may rotate; original dimensions are retained; local axes are identified in the anatomy. Each module remains within its permitted region. Envelope separation is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes, and enclosure allowance is at least 1 mm outside each solid envelope except at its functional opening. Functional openings are limited to camera, speakers and microphone; remaining module surfaces are enclosed. Batteries are enclosed envelopes. B01 uses a user-accessible cover, detachable connection and illustrated removal direction, with the required replacement-detail wording User-replaceable B01. U01 keeps its USB-C-shaped socket mouth exposed at the case wall. ### 3. Open for prototyping Spring travel, force and electrical protection remain to be prototyped. The glasses mass is a target, not yet measured. The following performance fields remain unspecified: component mass, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, optical prescription, waterproof rating and drop rating. U01 electrical fields remain unspecified: standard, power rating and charging protocol. Prototype topics include mass, fit/comfort, hinge life, thermal behaviour, charging reliability and capture/privacy interlock. Case materials and finishes are selected in the design, but any remaining finish approvals and production tolerances remain open until prototype review. ### 4. State and context decisions that are fixed The operating states are fixed. READY has an uncovered aperture, indicator off, and no active capture. CAPTURE has an uncovered aperture, a steadily white front capture indicator during the illustrated active interval, and active capture through the visible user-operated capture button. PRIVACY has the entire aperture covered by the opaque physical slider, indicator off, visible physical position mark, camera and microphone capture disabled, and capture inhibited. The wearing contexts are fixed for later boards: W1 everyday READY, W2 work pause PRIVACY, W3 commute pause READY, and W4 cafe pause PRIVACY. Product continuity across contexts is fixed: selected dimensions and component identities are shared across every context. --- ## Page 8 — Consequences for the next stage ### 1. Envelope integration rules The selected Continuum design applies the following integration rules to every recorded module envelope. There is at least 1 mm between separate envelopes. There is at least 1 mm outside every envelope except at its functional opening. Batteries are enclosed envelopes. The case and glasses shells, trays, liners, and supports are arranged so that no solid envelope is exposed except where a functional opening or an explicitly marked support or charging-contact interface requires local access. In the glasses, the minimum required separation is achieved at the C01-to-B02 envelope pair in the right temple, where the recorded envelopes are separated by 1.5 mm along the temple centreline after the selected placement. The C01-to-B02 gap is the tightest module-to-module separation in the glasses. The left temple keeps B01 and S01 separated by more than 1 mm, and the right temple keeps B02 and S02 separated by more than 1 mm. The front-frame pair K01 and I01 is separated by more than 1 mm while I01 remains centred 9.0 mm from the camera-aperture centre. M01 is placed on the left front-frame outer lower edge and is separated from K01, I01, and the hinge region by more than 1 mm. In the case, the minimum required separation is achieved at the CB01-to-CC01 envelope pair, where the selected placement provides 2.0 mm clearance. CC01 and U01 are separated by at least 2.0 mm, and U01’s socket mouth is the only exposed surface of that envelope. The 1 mm enclosure allowance is consumed by the shell in the sense that the innermost shell surface is offset at least 1 mm from each solid envelope, and the shell material and its compliant liners occupy the region outside that offset. In the right temple, the allowance around C01 and B02 is bounded by the inner TR90 shell and a thin compliant liner. In the left temple, the allowance around B01 and S01 is bounded by the inner TR90 shell. At the front frame, the allowance around K01 and I01 is bounded by the front shell except at the camera aperture and the indicator window. In the case, the allowance around CB01 and CC01 is bounded by the case shell and the flocked tray. At U01, the allowance terminates at the USB-C-shaped socket mouth. At the charging pads and case contact tips, the allowance is locally replaced by the explicitly marked support and charging-contact interfaces. --- ## Page 3 ### 4. Charging and docking interface The local charging interface is on the underside of the right temple. It uses exactly two flush circular pads, labelled P+ and P−. Each pad has a diameter of 2 mm. The pad centres are 6 mm apart along the temple. P+ is nearer the hinge, with its centre 18 mm behind the hinge axis. P− is nearer the tip, with its centre 24 mm behind the hinge axis. Both pad centres are within the first 60 mm from the hinge axis towards the tip. The pads are flush with the local temple surface. The case provides two contact tips. Each tip has a diameter of 1.2 mm. The tip centres are 6 mm apart. Polarity is aligned so that P+ mates with P+ and P− mates with P−. The contact faces are parallel at docking. A visible locating and keying feature identifies the matching orientation. The case has a keyed seat that receives the folded glasses. The formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm contact tips are the explicit marked local exceptions to the general enclosure and clearance rules. The case supports the frame and temple regions; the lenses are clear of direct supporting pressure. In the closed-lid relationship, all components are contained within the closed case. Removal access is provided by finger access to the frame and temple regions. The empty-case state presents an open cavity with the same supports, contacts, and locating feature. The docking state uses fully folded glasses with the privacy slider closed. In the charging state, the glasses are seated, both pads are mated, and the separate case indicator is steadily amber. In the stored or idle state, the same glasses are seated, the case indicator is off, and the case is closed. The case indicator is visible with the lid closed. Spring travel, force, and electrical protection remain to be prototyped. The U01 electrical fields of standard, power rating, and charging protocol also remain unspecified and must be resolved before production. --- ## Page 7 ### 8. Operating states and appurtenant changes The three operating states are READY, CAPTURE, and PRIVACY. The table below states the camera aperture, front capture indicator, control and capture behaviour, shutter position, camera availability, and microphone availability for each state. **Table 8-1 — Operating states** | State | Camera aperture | Front capture indicator | Control and capture behaviour | Shutter position | Camera availability | Microphone availability | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | READY | Uncovered | Off | Ready for deliberate user initiation; no active capture | Open, not covering the aperture | Available for capture when the user operates the capture button | Available for the user-initiated spoken question | | CAPTURE | Uncovered | Steadily white during the illustrated active interval | Visible user-operated capture button; active capture | Open, not covering the aperture | Available; active capture | Available for the user-initiated spoken question | | PRIVACY | Entire aperture covered by an opaque physical slider | Off | Visible physical position mark; camera and microphone capture disabled; pressing capture does not start capture | Closed over the aperture | Unavailable | Unavailable | The changes between states are precise. From READY to CAPTURE, the shutter remains open and the camera aperture remains uncovered; the front capture indicator changes from off to steadily white during the illustrated active interval; the camera becomes active for capture; the microphone remains available for the user-initiated spoken question; and the capture button initiates the active capture. From READY or CAPTURE to PRIVACY, the opaque slider moves 9 mm to the closed position over the camera; the front capture indicator remains off; the camera is unavailable; microphone capture is disabled; and pressing capture does not start capture. From PRIVACY to READY, the slider opens, the camera aperture becomes uncovered, the indicator remains off, and the camera and microphone become available again only for deliberate user initiation. The case behaviour is separate from the glasses state table. While charging, the case indicator is steadily amber. While stored or idle, the case indicator is off and the case is closed. The case indicator is visible with the lid closed. In the docked state, the folded glasses dock with the shutter closed. The bridge carries no docked indication until the tips make contact. Once the tips make contact and both pads are mated, the charging state can be indicated by the case indicator. --- ## Page 8 ### 9. B01 service arrangement B01 is the left battery envelope. It is located in the left temple, mid segment, 40 mm to 70 mm behind the hinge axis. The selected Continuum design provides a user-accessible cover on the left temple. The cover is flush with the satin TR90 shell in the closed position and is opened by the user without disturbing the optical front, the nose contact, or the ear contact. The battery envelope is an enclosed envelope during normal wear. The service arrangement exposes only the battery compartment when the cover is open. The battery connection is detachable. The battery is not soldered in place. The removal direction is illustrated. The illustrated removal direction shows the cover opening direction and the direction in which the battery envelope is withdrawn from its detachable connection. The marking text “User-replaceable B01” is placed beside the removal detail. The marking is visible when the cover is open and the removal detail is exposed. The service arrangement retains the required enclosure of B01 when the cover is closed. ### 10. Open items The following items remain to be prototyped and verified. They are not closed by this specification sheet. **10.1 Mass and comfort.** The mass target is 38 g, with a limit of not more than 42 g; the mass is unmeasured. Component masses, total glasses mass, total case mass, fit, comfort, nose-contact pressure, and ear-contact pressure remain to be prototyped and verified. **10.2 Hinge and folding.** Hinge life, folding order, folded-envelope repeatability, and the separation of the folded temple volumes remain to be verified. The selected dimensions are locked, but the hinge construction and folding order remain design choices within the Continuum direction. **10.3 Thermal and electrical.** Thermal behaviour, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, charging reliability, and electrical protection remain to be prototyped and verified. The U01 electrical fields of standard, power rating, and charging protocol remain unspecified. The charging interface spring travel and force remain to be prototyped. **10.4 Capture and privacy interlock.** The capture/privacy interlock remains to be prototyped and verified. Verification must confirm that pressing capture in PRIVACY does not start capture, that camera and microphone capture are disabled in PRIVACY, that the shutter travel is 9 mm, that the visible position mark is legible, and that I01 is visible when the shutter is closed. **10.5 Docking and case behaviour.** Verification must confirm the keyed seat, the P+ to P+ and P− to P− polarity alignment, the parallel contact faces, the 6 mm centre spacing of the pads and tips, the 18 mm and 24 mm pad-centre positions behind the hinge axis, and the 60 mm limit from the hinge axis. The case indicator must be verified as steadily amber while charging and off while stored or idle, and it must remain visible with the lid closed. **10.6 Envelope integration and tolerances.** Verification must confirm that every separate envelope maintains at least 1 mm separation after tolerance stack-up, that every solid envelope maintains at least 1 mm enclosure allowance except at its functional opening, and that the marked support and charging-contact interfaces are the only local exceptions. The case cavity clearance must be verified as 3.5 mm width, 6 mm depth, and 4 mm height per side, with a minimum of 2 mm on every opposing side, except at the formed docking seat and the two 1.2 mm contact tips. **10.7 Unspecified performance fields.** The following remain unspecified and must be resolved before production: optical prescription, waterproof rating, drop rating, battery capacity, runtime, charging time, component mass, and the U01 electrical standard, power rating, and charging protocol. **10.8 Material and colour application.** The colour palette is locked as LUMA-C01 Graphite (satin TR90), LUMA-C02 Bone (satin TR90), LUMA-C03 Silver (anodised aluminium), LUMA-C04 Smoke (silicone nose and ear contacts), and LUMA-C05 Warm Grey (flocked case tray). Colour codes, material applications, surface finishes, and the exact zoning of the satin TR90, anodised aluminium, silicone, and flocked tray must be recorded in the material and colour application deliverable. ---

material zone specification

# LUMA — Material Zoning and Finish Specification Sheet Selected direction: Continuum — seamless minimal. Deliverable: material-zone-specification. Tiers: 14, 24. Stage: process. Format: A4 presentation document, at least eight actual pages. This document contains no images. --- ## Page 1 ## Section 1 — Scope and zoning principle ### 1.1 Purpose of this sheet This sheet fixes the material zoning and finish specification for the selected Continuum direction of LUMA. It covers the complete glasses and the matching charging/storage case. It zones every surface into one of three families: exterior surfaces, interior and non-contact surfaces, and skin-contact surfaces. Each surface carries one material, one surface treatment and one colour code. The zoning is written for process stage, so it must be stable enough to guide later detailed design, tooling discussion and finish sampling. ### 1.2 Zoning families Exterior surfaces are the surfaces visible when the product is worn, carried, docked or stored. They include the outer front, outer temples, outer case, shutter slider, capture button, camera bezel, case meeting gap and socket surround. These surfaces carry the Continuum body colour and the satin family finish unless a functional opening interrupts them. Interior and non-contact surfaces are inside faces, service faces or functional lands that are not in sustained skin contact. They include the frame front interior, the inner front rim, lens edges, temple interiors, indicator windows, case tray, case seat and related internal surrounds. These surfaces may use the controlled Bone accent or the Warm Grey tray lining, but they do not introduce a second exterior body colour. Skin-contact surfaces are exactly four regions: left nose contact, right nose contact, left ear contact and right ear contact. These four regions use compliant silicone only. They are Smoke, soft matte, and have smooth rounded transitions into and out of each contact area. ### 1.3 One material, one treatment, one colour code Each surface in this sheet is assigned one material, one surface treatment and one colour code. The client-fixed materials are satin TR90 for the frame and temple shells, anodised aluminium for the hinge set, and silicone for the nose and ear contact surfaces. The colour choices are the developed Continuum palette recorded in Section 4 and repeated in locked form in Section 9. Functional optical, diffusing and contact surfaces are listed as functional surfaces; they do not add decorative colours to the palette. ### Table 1 — Zoning families and rules | Family | Surfaces | Rule | |---|---|---| | Exterior surfaces | Frame front exterior; left and right temple shell exteriors; temple tips; shutter slider; capture button; camera bezel; case exterior lid; case exterior body; case meeting gap; case input socket surround | One satin level across TR90. Graphite body colour. No gloss. No decorative metal except anodised aluminium. | | Interior and non-contact surfaces | Frame front interior; inner front rim; left and right temple shell interiors; lens edges; indicator windows; case interior tray; case seat; case indicator window | Controlled accents allowed: Bone inner rim, Warm Grey tray. Matte or satin as specified. No skin-contact silicone. | | Skin-contact surfaces | Left nose contact; right nose contact; left ear contact; right ear contact | Compliant silicone only. Smoke. Soft matte. Smooth rounded transitions. No sharp edges, ports or charging pads. | --- ## Page 2 ## Section 2 — Material schedule ### 2.1 Material and colour intent Table 2 is the material schedule. It lists the material or material/colour combination used in the Continuum direction. The commission fixes satin TR90, anodised aluminium and silicone. The case shell is selected as satin TR90 in Graphite so it matches the frame’s satin. The case tray and seat are flocked polymer in Warm Grey. The shutter slider and capture button are satin TR90 in Graphite. The colour choices are the developed Continuum palette, not client-fixed materials. ### Table 2 — Material schedule | Material | Application | Surface treatment | Colour code | Hex value | |---|---|---|---|---| | Satin TR90 — commission-fixed | Frame front and both temple shells; case exterior lid and body; shutter slider; capture button; camera bezel; case meeting gap; case input socket surround | Satin, low sheen, fine uniform texture; same on frame and temples | LUMA-C01 Graphite | #3A3D40 | | Satin TR90 — commission-fixed, Bone accent | Inner front rim | Satin, low sheen, fine uniform texture | LUMA-C02 Bone | #E7E3D8 | | Anodised aluminium — commission-fixed | Hinge set; case contact block | Fine matte metallic; no polished highlights | LUMA-C03 Silver | #B7BCC1 | | Silicone — commission-fixed | Nose-contact and ear-contact surfaces | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions; no sharp edges | LUMA-C04 Smoke | #6F7373 | | Flocked polymer — selected | Case interior tray and case seat | Flocked matte | LUMA-C05 Warm Grey | #B4AEA4 | | Clear optical polymer — fixed by shared facts | Two clear non-display lenses, lens edges | Polished optical edge; no decorative gloss | No applied colour — functional clear | N/A | | Diffuser polymer — selected | Indicator windows on glasses and case | Matte diffusing; non-glossy | No applied colour — functional diffuser | N/A | | Precious-metal contact plating — selected functional | Charging pads P+ and P−; case contact tips | Flush; fine matte contact surface | No applied decorative colour — functional contact | N/A | | Pad-print ink — selected | LUMA markings and User-replaceable B01 wording | Matte, satin-level, flush | LUMA-C02 Bone | #E7E3D8 | ### 2.2 Fixed and developed status The fixed materials are not open for substitution. Satin TR90 is fixed for the frame and temple shells. Anodised aluminium is fixed for the hinge set. Silicone is fixed for the nose and ear contact surfaces. The case shell material is selected as satin TR90 to match the frame’s satin. The tray is a flocked insert, not a gloss plastic. The shutter slider is satin TR90 so it reads as part of the front. The button is satin TR90 with a crisp edge, but its sheen remains the same satin level as the surrounding TR90. --- ## Page 3 ## Section 3 — Surface treatments ### 3.1 Treatment intent Surface treatments are specified so that a viewer sees one coherent object and a moulding engineer can inspect the tool and process. The TR90 satin finish is low sheen, with no visible moulding gloss and a fine uniform texture. It is the same on the frame and the temples. The anodised hinges are fine matte metallic, with no polished highlights. The silicone contact surfaces are soft matte, with smooth rounded transitions and no sharp edges. The case shell matches the frame’s satin. The case tray is a flocked matte. The shutter slider is satin so it reads as part of the front. The button is satin with a crisp edge. ### Table 3 — Surface treatment intent | Element | Treatment intent | Inspection check | |---|---|---| | TR90 satin finish | Low sheen; no visible moulding gloss; fine uniform texture; same on frame and temples | Check gloss level at 60°; no flow marks; texture uniform across front and temples. | | Anodised hinges | Fine matte metallic; no polished highlights | Check no bright buffed edges; uniform matte etch; colour within Silver. | | Silicone contact surfaces | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions; no sharp edges | Check radius at every transition; no flash; no glossy patches. | | Case shell | Matches the frame’s satin | Check case lid and body against frame under same light; no gloss mismatch. | | Case tray | Flocked matte | Check uniform fibre lay; no shiny areas; no loose flock. | | Shutter slider | Satin, reads as part of front | Check slider closed: tone and sheen match front; no proud gloss strip. | | Capture button | Satin with crisp edge | Check crisp perimeter; satin face; no polished bevel. | ### 3.2 Viewer and engineer checks The viewer check is coherence. The frame, temples, case shell, shutter and button must read as one satin family. The engineer check is reproducibility. There is one texture, one gloss target and one masking rule. The hinges must read as metal but not as jewellery. The silicone must read as soft and quiet. The tray must read as a lining, not as an exterior surface. The shutter must disappear into the front when closed. The button must be findable by touch without becoming a glossy accent. --- ## Page 4 ## Section 4 — Colour palette ### 4.1 Locked palette with developed hex mapping Table 4 records the locked Continuum palette. The codes and names are locked. The hex values are the developed production mapping used by this sheet for sampling and specification. ### Table 4 — Locked palette | Code | Name | Hex value | Application | |---|---|---|---| | LUMA-C01 | Graphite | #3A3D40 | Satin TR90, exterior shell of the glasses front, the temples and the case | | LUMA-C02 | Bone | #E7E3D8 | Satin TR90, inner front rim and all markings and prints | | LUMA-C03 | Silver | #B7BCC1 | Anodised aluminium hinges and the case contact block | | LUMA-C04 | Smoke | #6F7373 | Silicone nose and ear contact surfaces | | LUMA-C05 | Warm Grey | #B4AEA4 | Flocked case tray and seat | ### 4.2 Palette logic, part one Graphite is the body colour for both glasses and case so the family reads as one object. It carries the exterior shell, temples, case exterior, shutter, button and bezel. Bone is a single controlled interior accent used on the inner front rim and the markings. It is not used as a second exterior colour. Silver is reserved for metal only, so the aluminium reads as metal and nothing else pretends to be metal. ### 4.3 Palette logic, part two Smoke is the contact material, kept visually quiet because it is the only part in constant skin contact. Warm Grey is used for the tray so the interior reads as a lining rather than a surface. Functional optical, diffusing and contact interfaces are not decorative colours. They are listed in Section 6 without adding to the palette. No later stage may make Bone an exterior body colour, make Silver a decorative trim, or make Smoke a general-purpose dark accent. --- ## Page 5 ## Section 5 — Contact zoning ### 5.1 Four contact regions The shared wearer and contact-zone map gives exactly four skin-contact regions: left nose contact, right nose contact, left ear contact and right ear contact. Compliant silicone covers exactly these four regions. The silicone is LUMA-C04 Smoke, soft matte, with smooth rounded transitions into and out of every region. No other surface uses skin-contact silicone. ### 5.2 Transition and exclusion rules Every transition into and out of a contact region is a smooth rounded transition. There are no sharp edges, open ports or charging pads inside a skin-contact zone. The two charging pads are on the underside of the right temple, flush, diameter 2 mm, centres 6 mm apart, with P+ centre 18 mm and P- centre 24 mm behind the hinge axis, P+ nearer the hinge. They are outside the skin-contact zones. The button reach region is on the right temple; its surface is a non-contact exterior surface and follows the Graphite satin TR90 exterior rule. ### Table 5 — Contact zoning | Zone | Location | Material | Treatment | Colour | |---|---|---|---|---| | Left nose contact | Left nose-contact region from shared map | Silicone | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions | LUMA-C04 Smoke | | Right nose contact | Right nose-contact region from shared map | Silicone | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions | LUMA-C04 Smoke | | Left ear contact | Left ear-contact region from shared map | Silicone | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions | LUMA-C04 Smoke | | Right ear contact | Right ear-contact region from shared map | Silicone | Soft matte; smooth rounded transitions | LUMA-C04 Smoke | | Button reach region | Right temple, reachable while worn | Satin TR90 | Satin; crisp edge on button, same satin level | LUMA-C01 Graphite | | Charging pads — outside skin-contact zones | Underside of right temple; P+ centre 18 mm and P- centre 24 mm behind hinge axis | Precious-metal contact plating | Flush; fine matte contact surface | No applied decorative colour — functional contact | --- ## Page 6 ## Section 6 — Surface-by-surface application map ### 6.1 How to read the map Table 6 lists every visible surface of the glasses and the case named in the commission. low sheen | LUMA-C01 Graphite (#3A3D40) | | 21 | Case exterior body | Satin TR90 | Satin matching frame; low sheen | LUMA-C01 Graphite (#3A3D40) | | 22 | Case meeting gap | Satin TR90 | Satin matching frame; non-glossy | No applied colour — functional diffuser | ### 6.2 Treatment consistency across the map Across the map, every TR90 surface uses the same satin level. The only metal in the decorative finish is the anodised aluminium hinge set and the case contact block. The only silicone is at the four contact regions. The tray and seat are the only flocked surfaces. The shutter slider and button remain part of the satin TR90 family. Functional openings and windows do not become gloss accents. --- ## Page 8 ## Section 7 — Marking ### 7.1 Marking intent The required product marking is LUMA on the glasses and on the case. The required replacement-detail wording is User-replaceable B01. All markings use LUMA-C02 Bone on LUMA-C01 Graphite, are matte and sit at the same satin level as the TR90. They are durable pad prints. There is no raised badge, no polished insert and no second colour. Markings do not cross the hinge, do not touch skin-contact silicone and do not sit on the charging pads. ### Table 7 — Marking placement and method | Marking | Location | Method | Colour and material | |---|---|---|---| | LUMA on glasses | Inner surface of the right temple shell, 10 mm behind the hinge, centred on the temple centreline, 5 mm below the top edge | Durable matte pad print | LUMA-C02 Bone on LUMA-C01 Graphite | | LUMA on case | Case exterior lid, lower-right quadrant, 12 mm from the front edge and 10 mm from the side edge | Durable matte pad print | LUMA-C02 Bone on LUMA-C01 Graphite | | User-replaceable B01 | Inside the left temple shell, immediately beside the B01 user-accessible cover, aligned with the illustrated removal direction | Durable matte pad print; beside the removal-direction illustration | LUMA-C02 Bone on LUMA-C01 Graphite | ### 7.2 Placement rules The B01 marking is not placed on silicone, not on the charging pads and not across a hinge. The B01 cover is user-accessible, has a detachable connection and an illustrated removal direction; the wording sits on the flat land beside that detail. The case marking is outside the meeting gap and does not interfere with the locating/keying feature. All markings remain visible with the relevant cover or lid in its normal service position. The marking ink is matte and flush, so it does not create a gloss patch against the satin TR90. --- ## Page 9 ## Section 8 — Finish consistency rules ### 8.1 Consistency rules The following rules keep the family coherent. They apply to process and final stages. No later stage may introduce an additional finish or colour. 1. One satin level across every TR90 part. Frame front, both temple shells, case shell, shutter slider, capture button, camera bezel, case meeting gap and socket surround use the same satin TR90 finish. 2. Metal only where it is aluminium. Decorative metal is anodised aluminium in LUMA-C03 Silver on the hinge set and case contact block. Functional contact interfaces are not decorative and do not introduce a second metal colour. 3. Silicone only at the four contact regions. Nose and ear contact surfaces use LUMA-C04 Smoke silicone. No other surface uses skin-contact silicone. 4. Bone used only for the interior accent and markings. Inner front rim and all markings and prints use LUMA-C02 Bone. Bone is not an exterior body colour. 5. No additional finish or colour introduced at any later stage. No gloss, chrome, soft-touch coating, secondary paint, sticker or lens tint is added to the Continuum direction. 6. The case shell matches the frame’s satin. The case must not read as gloss, rubberised or fabric. 7. The case tray and seat are flocked matte in Warm Grey. They must not be changed to moulded gloss or hard plastic. 8. The shutter slider remains satin so it reads as part of the front. It must not become a glossy black window or a metallic strip. 9. The capture button remains satin with a crisp edge. It must not acquire a polished bevel or a different satin level. 10. All transitions into and out of skin-contact zones are smooth rounded transitions. No sharp edge, open port or charging pad lies inside a skin-contact zone. 11. Functional optical, diffusing and contact surfaces are listed as functional. They are not palette colours and must not be used to introduce a new accent. --- ## Page 10 ## Section 9 — Colour codes in the locked schedule ### 9.1 Locked palette rows reproduced exactly The locked schedule palette rows are reproduced below exactly, character for character, so the codes match the component and state specification sheet. - Colour palette: LUMA-C01 Graphite (satin TR90, exterior shell of the glasses front, the temples and the case), LUMA-C02 Bone (satin TR90, inner front rim and all markings and prints), LUMA-C03 Silver (anodised aluminium hinges and the case contact block), LUMA-C04 Smoke (silicone nose and ear contact surfaces), LUMA-C05 Warm Grey (flocked case tray and seat). ### 9.2 Relationship to Section 4 The hex values recorded in Section 4 are the developed production mapping for these locked codes. They do not alter the locked row text above. The codes, names and applications in this section are the reference values to be carried into the component and state specification sheet. No other palette codes are introduced by this material zoning and finish specification.
